extension.description: Automatically mutes bad words during video playback using subtitle timing. Works with local files and streaming add-ons such as ororo.tv.
extension.disclaimer: Mute accuracy depends on subtitle timing.
extension.news: 1.8.1: - Fix subtitles re-appearing during filtering on streaming add-ons (e.g. ororo on a Google Streamer): after the add-on reads the subtitle data and hides the text, some sources re-enable subtitles on their own. The add-on now keeps watching the subtitle state for the rest of the session and re-hides them every second, so profanity never flickers back onto the screen. 1.8.0: - Automatic scene-skipping data: the add-on can now fetch scene-skip timestamps by movie from a hosted JSON file (no files needed on the device — works on a Google Streamer / Android TV box). The video is identified from Kodi's metadata (Player.GetItem) for streaming, or from the file/URL for local content. Set the URL in Settings (defaults to the repo's published skipdata.json) and add entries keyed by movie title, plus an optional "default" entry. 1.7.1: - Fix "tried to force subtitles on but none became active" on streaming sources (e.g. Google Streamer + ororo): enabling an external subtitle is asynchronous, so the add-on now re-requests it inside the retry loop and re-selects the exposed track by index with enable=true until it becomes active, instead of giving up after a single attempt. - On Android/Streamer devices where a source never exposes a subtitle track while subtitles are off, the on-screen diagnostic now clearly distinguishes "a track was exposed but wouldn't stick" from "the source provides no subtitle for this video", so the cause is easy to understand. 1.7.0: - New: scene skipping. When enabled, the add-on jumps past flagged scenes (scary, intense, mature) instead of only muting. Scene windows are read from simple offline skip lists you edit yourself — no subscription or external service needed. - Skip lists live in special://profile/addon_data/service.profanity.filter/skiplists/ and match by movie name (e.g. "Avatar (2009).skip.txt") or global.skip.txt for every video. Format is one "start end" per line (mm:ss / h:mm:ss / plain seconds). A bundled example is included. - New settings: "Enable scene skipping" and "Skip-start lookahead (seconds)". 1.6.1: - Fix streaming subtitle discovery: subtitle URLs with signed query strings (e.g. ororo WebVTT tokens) are now kept intact so downloads no longer fail with auth errors. - Fall back to scanning the full Kodi log when the subtitle URL falls outside the recent log tail. - Adds a "Show detailed failure diagnostics" setting that shows the exact failing stage on screen (player id, whether subtitles became active, URL/download/parse results) so issues are easy to report without reading Kodi's log. 1.6.0: - Subtitles are no longer shown on screen. The filter works with subtitles switched off: local files are read from disk directly (never displayed), and streaming subtitles are only enabled long enough to capture the timing data, then hidden again. - The "Hide subtitles after scanning" setting has been removed — profanity text is always kept off the screen. 1.5.0: - Fix false positives caused by overly greedy wildcards (sh*t no longer matches "shift", c*nt no longer matches "count"). - Ship a curated word list. Innocent/common words (god, hell, abuse, etc.) are no longer muted by default. - Use the active video player for subtitle discovery instead of a hardcoded player id.
